speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how many weeks pregnant you are, and approximately how much blood have you lost? Also, is the pain in your lower abdomen sharp or cramping?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your previous cesarean section, the sudden severe pain, and the bleeding after contractions stopped, I am very concerned about a uterine rupture. Is the pain constant and located specifically at the site of your old scar, and do you feel any fetal parts more easily than before?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of a prior cesarean and the sudden cessation of contractions with severe pain, I am highly concerned for a uterine rupture. Can you tell me if the fetus has stopped moving or if you feel any unusual softness or loss of shape in your abdomen? REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Monitoring

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring shows recurrent variable decelerations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recurrent variable decelerations and your severe pain confirm an obstetric emergency, likely uterine rupture or placental abruption. Do you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or have you passed out, which would suggest you are going into shock? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound; REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis findings suggest a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum. Complete Blood Count (Hematology) shows Hemoglobin at 10.2 g/dL (decreased) and Platelets at 200,000 /μL. Vital Signs indicate Pulse of 110/min, Blood Pressure of 90/60 mm Hg, and Respiratory Rate of 17/min. Abdominal examination reveals mild distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic sound predominating, and diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Obstetric examination notes no contractions felt at the time of examination.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirming a uterine wall disruption, combined with your signs of shock and the cessation of contractions, makes the diagnosis clear. I must immediately prepare you for an emergency laparotomy to repair the rupture and deliver the baby. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture.
